blogTitle: How to Choose Your Interior Design Style
videoTitle: How to Choose Your Interior Design Style
script:
How to Choose Your Interior Design Style

[warmly] You know that feeling when you've decorated a room yourself… loved every single piece when you bought it… but together something just feels OFF?

That's almost always because you don't yet have a clear sense of your OWN interior design style — and honestly, once you crack it, everything becomes so much easier.

Here's the thing — when you know your style, you stop buying things you later regret… every purchase has a CLEAR purpose, and your home starts to feel genuinely coherent.

So here's my step-by-step — start by gathering every image you've SAVED… your phone photos, Pinterest boards, magazine clippings — don't filter, just pull them all together.

After about twenty or thirty images, PATTERNS emerge — are the rooms light or dark? Minimal or layered? Natural textures or sleek surfaces? Write three words that describe the mood.

[curious] A little exercise I love — walk through your own home right now, look at what you already OWN with fresh eyes… the pieces you've kept longest are telling you everything.

Now — the big overview… the most popular styles you might recognise in yourself: Scandi minimal, Japandi, bohemian, mid-century modern, industrial, coastal, maximalist… each has its OWN visual language.

Here's something people don't realise — the wall art you're instinctively drawn to is basically a MAP of your style… your choices are never as random as they feel.

Clean lines and monochrome prints? That's a minimal instinct. Warm botanicals and earthy tones? That's boho or Japandi speaking… trust me — your art choices don't LIE.

[excited] And this is the fun bit — once you KNOW your style, choosing wall art and home decor stops being guesswork and starts being genuinely enjoyable… like speaking a language you finally understand.

A practical rule — always let your wall art ECHO the room's palette… pick out one colour from a print and repeat it in a cushion, a vase, a throw… that's what makes a space feel intentional.

Room by room — your living room sets the TONE for the whole home, so start there… it's where your chosen style should be clearest and most confidently expressed.

The bedroom can be a slightly softer, MORE intimate version of your style… and don't underestimate hallways — they're the first impression, so they deserve just as much thought.

[sighs] The biggest mistake I see? Buying pieces you love IN ISOLATION… without asking whether they speak the same visual language as everything else in the room.

Other mistakes to avoid — chasing trends that don't actually suit YOU, or trying to copy a whole look exactly… your home should feel like YOU, not like a showroom.

Now — you can absolutely BLEND styles, and most great rooms do… the key is to pick ONE dominant style and let the second one add texture and personality, never compete with it.

A good rule for blending — keep your PALETTE consistent even if your influences vary… colour is the thread that holds different styles together without the room feeling chaotic.

[warmly] For a bit of real inspiration — clean black-and-white line art is one of the most versatile starting points… it works beautifully in minimal and Scandi spaces and pulls a room together instantly.

Abstract sets are another brilliant option — especially if your style is modern or eclectic… THREE prints at once gives you an instant gallery wall that feels considered, not accidental.

[excited] If your instincts run bohemian or earthy… these warm, figurative women prints are honestly one of my FAVOURITES — they bring so much soul and warmth to a living room wall.

Drawn to geometry and a more spiritual, structured feel? Sacred geometry sets are perfect for that — they add DEPTH and intention to a room without overwhelming it.

And for a more sculptural, classical-modern look — these sculpture prints are quietly STUNNING… they suit minimal and transitional spaces beautifully and always feel refined.

[gently] So — start with what you're ALREADY drawn to… pay attention to those instincts, find the patterns, name your style, and let your wall art be the thing that ties it all together.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
hero: A beautifully art-directed Scandi-minimal living room bathed in soft natural daylight streaming through a large window. Warm white walls, a low linen sofa in soft greige, a pale oak coffee table with a stack of design books and a ceramic vase holding dried pampas grass, a woven jute rug, and a set of two framed black-and-white art prints on the wall as the clear focal point. The palette is calm — warm white, soft grey, pale oak, muted black accents. The room feels curated, intentional, and deeply liveable. A stylish woman in her 30s stands slightly off-centre looking thoughtfully at the wall art, coffee cup in hand, relaxed and at home. Five variations: same room and styling, only the person or their position changes — seated on the sofa, standing closer to the art, turned toward camera, crouching to style the coffee table.
